lee: heads-up: nightly canary shows increased p99 on streaming-chat. investigating now, flamegraph points to host parse/tokenize and grpc writev hot spots. snapshot: https://perf.internal/runs/7991001 :frowning:

tara: which commit landed last night? any tokenizer or kernel-selector PRs?

lee: two commits: emoji-normalize in tokenizer and kernel-metadata refresh (added compat kernels for safety). suspect interaction. perf top sample:
```
18.7% host::parse_stream
16.2% tokenizer::tokenize_normalize
13.5% grpc::WriteV
10.4% kernel_selector::choose_fallback
7.8% kvcache::evict
6.0% http2::serialize_frames
```

ben: the kernel metadata change added a fallback path for sequences > 1k to avoid quantized fast-paths. choose_fallback is heavier. if batching mixes lengths, we may be triggering it often.

olivia: kvcache metrics show an evict burst ~23:10 UTC and hit_rate dropped 12pts. timeline aligns with deploy. Could tokenizer normalization have changed prefix hashes?

lee: yes — the emoji-normalize change collapses certain unicode sequences which inadvertently altered prefix keys for the kvcache. keys shifted, causing many misses and evictions.

tara: that explains higher CPU: more tokenization + more backend kernel work + increased writev overhead when responses get larger.

ben: short-term options:
- set per-request flag to skip heavy normalization on hot path (fast-path)
- add batch split rule: if any seq_len > 512, split batch to avoid mixed-length batches
- temporarily prefer old kernel scoring (force quantized kernels when safe)

lee: I pushed a small canary for batch-splitting (max_mixed_batch=6) and added debug logs for kernel selection reasons. rolling now.

olivia: opened PR to make tokenizer normalization produce stable prefix hashes: keep legacy hash version as a fallback. PR: https://git/redwood/pr/4521

bench-bot: local perf snippet:
```
baseline: p95=110ms p99=200ms qps=460
canary: p95=135ms p99=260ms qps=440
canary+batch-split: p95=115ms p99=205ms qps=455
```

ben: nice improvement with batch-split. still want to avoid reverting normalization entirely. better to make kvcache tolerant to key-version bumps.

tara: suggestion: add a token_key_version tag to kvcache entries and allow read-through for last N versions for a short warmup window. avoids mass misses on deploy.

lee: adding ticket: INF-2217 "kvcache multi-version read window". also INF-2218 "kernel selector: batch-composition aware scoring".

olivia: I'll prep a small change to bump hot-key allocation so evictions won't thrash cross-shard. also adding eviction-alerting to page on >10/min during deploy windows.

ben: long-term: consider isolating long-sequence requests into dedicated worker pools or separate queues so kernel selection and batching don't affect short-request latency.

lee: agreed. added to roadmap and created INF-2219 for long-seq isolation experiments.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started (deploy/799101). monitoring channels enabled.

bench-bot: running ABs, will post updated p95/p99 in 10m.

lee: thanks all. immediate plan: keep batch-split canary, apply tokenizer fallback hash, implement kvcache multi-version read for rollout window. will follow up with graphs. :thumbsup:
